# cfqt: the research description classified on the CFQT content map (first = main topic, '-' = outside the map); counts as one piece of evidence.

column3: Quantum topology, geometric quantization of moduli spaces, topological quantum field theory and resurgence; quantum algorithms and software for optimization, differential equations, communication and error correction.
Algebraic topology: homotopy theory and operads.
Mathematics behind quantum theory: topological quantum field theory, topological quantum computing, differential geometry and topology; directs SDU's MSc programme in quantum computing.
Theoretical particle physics and gravity: quantum field theory and scattering amplitudes; leads the Scattering Amplitudes Group.
Bridges foundational quantum mathematics and quantum technology: advanced quantum sampling techniques for digital computation and analogue simulation (Andersen team).

Gaussian Boson Sampling: algorithms, applications and theoretical advantages of photonic quantum computing, building on a GBS-based clustering algorithm and work on bosonic quantum error-correcting codes.

Benchmarking quantum algorithms against classical ones with a rigorous mathematical approach, from quantum machine learning (quantum kernels, hybrid neural networks) to wider applications (Andersen team).
Use cases for Gaussian Boson Sampling, especially estimating high-dimensional integrals (DEiC postdoc scholarship in quantum algorithms, with J. E. Andersen and S. Shan).

Non-perturbative formulations of perturbative quantum field theories, especially Chern-Simons theory in the BV formalism, using higher category theory and derived geometry (PhD with K. Wernli and J. E. Andersen).
Algorithms, advantages and applications of Gaussian Boson Sampling as a model of photonic quantum computing (PhD with J. E. Andersen and S. Shan).
